learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected seven newtons and locked it in.
observations.exploration: At ninety degrees resultant five N and fifty-three degrees north of east. Home zero degrees gave seven N east; End one-eighty gave one N west. Swapped tip-to-tail order; metrics unchanged. Stepped back through angle range, observed one-sixty-five degrees with one-point-three N at one-thirty degrees, then restored ninety and five N.
observations.reveal: Corrected to five N, explained tip-to-tail addition and right-triangle formula. Described aligned seven and opposed one boundaries, plus a supplied one-oh-five-degree four-point-three N comparison. Frictionless ice and only two horizontal pulls stated.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Opposed arrows gave westward orange resultant; swapped right-angle construction showed north then east with same diagonal endpoint. Labels and explanation readable.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Concrete simultaneous-force prediction targets adding magnitudes without direction.
prediction.evidence: Seven chosen against five and one.

interaction.reason: Angle endpoints and order swap distinguish direction and commutativity.
interaction.evidence: Seven aligned, one opposed, five perpendicular; swap unchanged.

payoff.reason: Reveal connects arrows and right-triangle arithmetic with tested boundaries.
payoff.evidence: Square root of three squared plus four squared.

clarity.reason: Tip-to-tail labels and resultant magnitude/direction align.
clarity.evidence: Order swapped same single force caption; frictionless assumption.

transfer.reason: General arrow-addition rule stated without a new application.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard angle endpoints and steps worked; screen reader, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: Three plus four can give five when directions differ.

visualExplanation.reason: Arrow construction shows both magnitude and direction.
visualExplanation.evidence: Orange diagonal with swapped gray components.

playfulness.reason: Rotating force and swapping order invite geometric exploration.

depth.reason: Links vector addition, commutativity and Pythagorean magnitude.
depth.evidence: Different angle, same component magnitudes, different resultant.

complexity.reason: One geometric control introduces vector magnitude and direction.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Add directed quantities rather than their lengths and interpret tip-to-tail construction.
complexity.interfaceBurden: One stepped angle slider and order swap.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Resultant force, newtons and vector addition.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Degrees from east, N and squared-root relation.

whyCool: The total follows the arrow endpoint, not the sum of rope magnitudes.
caveat: Two-force frictionless model excludes other forces; supplied one-oh-five-degree reveal value was not separately inspected in a settled exploration state.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
